Align protein sequences with mzLib, and map every residue onto the other sequence

proteins_align.Rd

Align protein sequences pairwise with mzLib's global affine-gap aligner, and map every residue of each sequence to its counterpart in the other, or to none.

Answers where is residue 120 of this protein in its isoform, its ortholog, or last year's entry? A position means something only in the sequence it was counted in, and counting the same number along the other sequence is wrong after the first insertion or deletion. This aligns each pair with mzLib's PairwiseAligner.Align (mzLib #1428) and maps every residue to its counterpart in the other sequence, or to NA when it has none.

Usage

proteins_align(pairs, gap_open = NULL, gap_extend = NULL, end_gaps = NULL,
  max_cells = NULL, residue_map = TRUE, timeout = NULL)

Arguments

pairs

A list of c(source, target) character vectors of one-letter sequences, one result row each, in order: list(c(canonical, isoform)) for one pair. Map(c, sources, targets) builds the list from two vectors. Sent to mzLib exactly as given (case is kept, and compared case-insensitively). Either sequence may be empty, not both. mzLib refuses - and .; it scores any other letter BLOSUM62 does not name (U, O, a digit, a space) as X, so strip modifications first.

gap_open

Cost of opening a gap, in BLOSUM62's half-bits, charged once per gap: a gap of k residues costs gap_open + k * gap_extend. NULL (the default) sends nothing, and mzLib's default applies: 11 half-bits. mzLib refuses a negative value.

gap_extend

Cost of each residue in a gap, the first included, in half-bits. NULL (the default): mzLib's, 1 half-bit. mzLib refuses less than 1.

end_gaps

"free" - a gap at either end of either sequence costs nothing, so a signal peptide or a longer tail on one side is not penalised - or "charged". NULL (the default): mzLib's, "free".

max_cells

The largest table mzLib will build, (nchar(source) + 1) * (nchar(target) + 1) cells of one byte each. A larger pair is refused rather than allowed to exhaust memory. NULL (the default): mzLib's, 200,000,000 cells (about 200 MB). Two titin isoforms need about 1.2 billion; mzLib accepts up to 2,147,483,591.

residue_map

TRUE (the default) returns residue_map, one row per residue of both sequences. FALSE sends --no-residue-map and returns only the pairs table, for a large batch where you want the scores and counts.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL (the default) to wait.

Details

It is a global alignment with affine gaps (Gotoh's form of Needleman-Wunsch), scored with BLOSUM62. All the pairs are aligned in one bridge call, in order, so a few thousand isoform pairs cost one process start.

Every option you leave out is mzLib's to set. mzLibR sends nothing for it, and the result says what the aligner used (gap_open, gap_extend, end_gaps, max_cells). mzLib's defaults in the pinned build are gap open 11, gap extend 1, free end gaps and a 200,000,000-cell limit: BLASTP's gap costs for BLOSUM62, and EMBOSS needle's free end gaps.

Value

An mzlibr_alignments. aligner_id is mzLib's name for the method and every parameter, e.g. "global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=free": store it with any position you map, so the mapping says how it was made. matrix is always "BLOSUM62". gap_open and gap_extend are the gap costs used, in BLOSUM62's half-bits; end_gaps the end-gap rule used; max_cells the table limit used, in cells: yours, or mzLib's default when you gave none. record_count counts the pairs aligned. caveats says what the score and the mapping do and do not mean.

records is a data.frame with one row per pair, in input order: pair_index (1-based in R, so it indexes pairs); source_length and target_length in residues; score, the BLOSUM62 score in half-bits (see the traps); identical and substituted, the paired residues that are the same letter and that differ, in residues; source_residues_facing_gap and target_residues_facing_gap, the residues with no counterpart, in residues; and aligned_source and aligned_target, each sequence with - wherever it faces a residue of the other across a gap, the same length, to print one above the other.

residue_map is a data.frame with one row per residue of each sequence, pair by pair, each pair's source residues first and then its target residues: pair_index (1-based); sequence, "source" or "target"; position, 1-based in that sequence, as in mzLib and UniProt; residue, as given; mapped_position, the 1-based position of its counterpart in the other sequence, **NA when it faces a gap, never the nearest residue**; and mapped_residue, the counterpart's letter (NA facing a gap), a different letter from residue on a substitution. It is NULL with residue_map = FALSE.

Reading one position

proteins_map_source_to_target and proteins_map_target_to_source look positions up for one pair; proteins_alignments splits a result into one mzlibr_alignment per pair for them. They read the residue map mzLib's TryMapSourceToTarget and TryMapTargetToSource filled, and compute nothing.

The traps

**score is not an identity, a bit score or an E-value.** It is a raw sum of BLOSUM62 scores in half-bits, less the gaps, and it grows with length. Compare scores only between alignments with the same aligner_id. mzLibR computes no percent identity, because there are several definitions: divide identical by the length you mean.

It is a global alignment. Every residue of both sequences is placed, paired or facing a gap. With free end gaps a short sequence is placed on the best-scoring stretch of a long one, even when it has no real match there.

One optimal alignment, chosen the same way every time. Where two alignments score the same, mzLib's traceback picks one, always the same one. DYNC1I2 isoform 2B is a real case: canonical V76 and V82 are both V, either could pair with the isoform's V76, and mzLib pairs V82.

Always check the residue at a mapped position before carrying a modification across: a phosphosite on S is not a site on A. mapped_residue sits beside residue for that.

Wraps

Wire verb proteins align. Generated from the bridge's verb spec proteins.align.yaml (bridge commit 84c3b984b6b9) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • PairwiseAligner in mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PairwiseAligner.Align in mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PairwiseAligner.Id in mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAligner.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PairwiseAlignment.TryMapSourceToTarget in mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAlignment.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PairwiseAlignment.TryMapTargetToSource in mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/PairwiseAlignment.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SubstitutionMatrix.Blosum62 in mzLib/Omics/SequenceAlignment/SubstitutionMatrix.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

pairs

string[]; required; range >= 1 pair; each line exactly one tab. Read from stdin (not an option): one pair per line, the source sequence, a tab, the target sequence, as one-letter residue codes. Each sequence reaches mzLib exactly as given, case and all. Either sequence may be empty, but not both, because a blank line is skipped. One row per line, in input order, duplicates included. Sequences always travel on stdin, never argv: two titin isoforms are about 70,000 characters, past argv's 32 KB ceiling on Windows.

gap_open (wire --gap-open)

int; in half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units); default 11; range >= 0 (mzLib refuses a negative value). The cost of opening a gap, charged once per gap. A gap of length k costs gap-open plus k times gap-extend, BLAST's convention. Absent: nothing is sent and mzLib's PairwiseAligner default applies, which is 11 at d10017ce (BLASTP's default with BLOSUM62).

gap_extend (wire --gap-extend)

int; in half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units); default 1; range >= 1 (mzLib refuses 0 or less). The cost of each residue in a gap, the first included. Absent: mzLib's default, 1 at d10017ce.

end_gaps (wire --end-gaps)

string; default free; range free | charged (case-insensitive). free: a gap at either end of either sequence costs nothing, so one sequence may overhang the other (a signal peptide, a longer C-terminus) without penalty, as EMBOSS needle scores end gaps by default. charged: every gap costs. mzLib's PairwiseAligner.FreeEndGaps, true or false. Absent: mzLib's default, free (true) at d10017ce. The spelling is mzLib's own, from its aligner id.

max_cells (wire --max-cells)

int; in cells; default 2e+08; range 1 to 2147483591 (Array.MaxLength; mzLib refuses anything outside). The largest dynamic-programming table mzLib will build, (source length + 1) x (target length + 1) cells of one byte each. A larger pair is refused rather than allowed to exhaust memory. Absent: mzLib's default, 200,000,000 cells (about 200 MB) at d10017ce.

residue_map (wire --no-residue-map)

flag; default FALSE. Leave out the residue map (residue_map is then null). The pairs table is unchanged. For a batch where only the scores and counts are wanted: the map has one row per residue of both sequences.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

aligner_id

string; never NA. mzLib's PairwiseAligner.Id, naming the method and every parameter, e.g. global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=free. Store it with any mapped position.

matrix

string; never NA. The substitution matrix's name, always BLOSUM62: mzLib's default, the only one the wire offers.

gap_open

int; in half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units); never NA. The gap-open cost the aligner used: the option's value, or mzLib's default when it was absent.

gap_extend

int; in half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units); never NA. The gap-extension cost the aligner used.

end_gaps

string; never NA. free or charged: the end-gap rule the aligner used.

max_cells

int; in cells; never NA. The table limit the aligner used.

record_count

int; in pairs; never NA. Rows: the input pairs.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The pairs table's columns in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. Column name to one value per pair, in input order.

residue_map

object; NA when --no-residue-map was given. {row_count, column_names, columns}: one row per residue of each sequence of each pair, pair by pair, each pair's source residues (positions 1 to its length) and then its target residues (typed under result.tables.residue_map).

caveats

string[]; never NA. Seven static caveats.

Columns of records

pair_index

int; never NA. 0-based position of the pair among the non-blank stdin lines.

source_length

int; in residues; never NA. The source sequence's length.

target_length

int; in residues; never NA. The target sequence's length.

score

int; in half-bits (BLOSUM62 score units); never NA. PairwiseAlignment.Score: substitution scores summed over the paired residues, less every charged gap. A raw score, not a bit score, an E-value or an identity; compare it only between alignments with the same aligner_id.

identical

int; in residues; never NA. Paired residues that are the same letter, compared case-insensitively (PairwiseAlignment.Identical).

substituted

int; in residues; never NA. Paired residues that differ (PairwiseAlignment.Substituted).

source_residues_facing_gap

int; in residues; never NA. Source residues with no target counterpart: an extra or deleted stretch, or an overhang.

target_residues_facing_gap

int; in residues; never NA. Target residues with no source counterpart.

aligned_source

string; never NA. The source as given with '-' wherever it faces a target residue across a gap; as long as aligned_target.

aligned_target

string; never NA. The target as given with '-' wherever it faces a source residue across a gap.

Fields of residue_map

pair_index

int; never NA. The pair the residue belongs to.

sequence

string; never NA. source or target: which sequence position is in.

position

int; never NA. 1-based position in that sequence, as everywhere in mzLib.

residue

string; never NA. The residue at position, one letter, as given.

mapped_position

int; NA when the residue faces a gap, so it has no counterpart (mzLib's TryMap returned false); never the nearest residue. 1-based position of the paired residue in the other sequence: TryMapSourceToTarget for a source row, TryMapTargetToSource for a target row.

mapped_residue

string; NA when the residue faces a gap. The paired residue, one letter, as given. Different from residue on a substitution.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

no pairs on stdin; a line that is not exactly two tab-separated fields (the message names the pair)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--gap-open, --gap-extend or --max-cells not an integer, or given without a value; a value mzLib's PairwiseAligner constructor refuses (gap-open below 0, gap-extend below 1, max-cells below 1 or above 2147483591), with mzLib's message and the option named; --end-gaps not free or charged, or given without a value

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refused a pair: a sequence holding a gap character ('-' or '.'), or a table larger than max-cells. The message names the pair and quotes mzLib, which gives the cell count. The whole call fails on the first such pair, in input order.

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never seen at d10017ce: mzLib's aligner throws nothing else for non-null input

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • score is a raw substitution-matrix score in BLOSUM62's half-bit units, summed over the alignment: it grows with length and is not a bit score, an E-value or a percent identity. Compare scores only between alignments with the same aligner_id.

  • Global alignment: every residue of both sequences is in the alignment, paired or facing a gap. With end gaps free (mzLib's default) an overhang at either end costs nothing, so a short sequence is placed on the best-scoring stretch of a long one even when it has no real match there.

  • A residue facing a gap has no counterpart: its mapped_position is null, never the nearest residue.

  • One optimal alignment is returned. Where several score the same, mzLib's traceback prefers a residue pair, then a gap in the target, then a gap in the source, so the same input always gives the same alignment; a residue beside an indel may sit on the other side of the gap in another aligner's equally good answer. DYNC1I2 isoform 2B lacks six residues of the canonical sequence: V76 and V82 of the canonical are both V, either could pair with the isoform's V76, and mzLib pairs V82.

  • mzLib refuses only the gap characters '-' and '.'. Any other character BLOSUM62 does not name (selenocysteine U, pyrrolysine O, J, a digit, a space, a bracket) is scored as X, so pass bare one-letter sequences. Letters are compared case-insensitively; aligned_source, aligned_target and the residue columns keep the case given.

  • Time and memory grow with the product of the two lengths: mzLib builds a (source length + 1) x (target length + 1) table of one byte per cell and refuses a pair larger than max_cells. Two identical sequences free of X and * are aligned residue for residue without the table, so max_cells does not limit them.

  • Each stdin line is one pair, aligned in input order; blank lines are skipped. mzLib's aligner takes no thread count, so pairs are aligned one after another.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.proteins.align_many

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::proteins::align_with with AlignOptions

  • R (mzLibR): proteins_align

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • A substitution matrix other than BLOSUM62 is not offered. mzLib can read one (SubstitutionMatrix.Parse(name, TextReader), NCBI's text format), but it needs a name for the aligner id, which the bridge would have to invent, and the units of every score would then be that matrix's. Whether to add --matrix FILE, and where its name comes from, is open.

  • mzLib scores any character BLOSUM62 does not name as X, digits and spaces included, so a sequence with a stray modification bracket or a number aligns without complaint. Whether PairwiseAligner.Align should refuse non-letters, as it refuses '-' and '.', is an mzLib question, not raised upstream yet.

  • Pairs are aligned one at a time: PairwiseAligner takes no degree of parallelism, so the wire has no --threads (PARALLELISM.md). A batch aligner with one (for proteome-wide ortholog or isoform maps) would be an mzLib addition.

  • residue_map is not validated by tools/check_verbs.py, which checks only 'columns' and 'bulk'. The bridge test ADeletion_LeavesItsResiduesUnmappedAndMapsAcrossTheGap pins its column order.

  • Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.

References

  • doi:10.1016/0022-2836(70)90057-4: Global alignment by dynamic programming (Needleman and Wunsch 1970, J Mol Biol 48:443)

  • doi:10.1016/0022-2836(82)90398-9: Affine gap costs in the same time and memory order, the form mzLib implements (Gotoh 1982, J Mol Biol 162:705)

  • doi:10.1073/pnas.89.22.10915: BLOSUM62, the substitution matrix and its half-bit units (Henikoff and Henikoff 1992, PNAS 89:10915)

See also

proteins_map_source_to_target, proteins_read with sequences = TRUE for the sequences of a database

Examples


# mzLib's own deletion case: QRQ (source 9 to 11) is missing from the target.
aln <- proteins_align(list(c("MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ", "MKTAYIAKISFVKSHFSRQ")))
aln
#> <mzlibr_alignments> 1 pair(s), global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=free
#>   pair 1: score 80 half-bits, 19 identical, 0 substituted, 3 + 0 facing a gap
#>   residue map: 41 rows; NA mapped_position faces a gap
writeLines(c(aln$records$aligned_source, aln$records$aligned_target))
#> MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ
#> MKTAYIAK---ISFVKSHFSRQ
aln$records[, c("score", "identical", "source_residues_facing_gap")]
#>   score identical source_residues_facing_gap
#> 1    80        19                          3
proteins_map_source_to_target(aln, 8:12)
#> [1]  8 NA NA NA  9

# Two pairs in one call; the free overhang MLLL faces a gap.
alns <- proteins_align(list(c("MKTAYIAKQRQISFVKSHFSRQ", "MKTAYIAKISFVKSHFSRQ"),
                            c("MLLLPEPTIDE", "PEPTIDE")))
alns$records[, c("pair_index", "score", "aligned_target")]
#>   pair_index score         aligned_target
#> 1          1    80 MKTAYIAK---ISFVKSHFSRQ
#> 2          2    39            ----PEPTIDE
proteins_map_source_to_target(proteins_alignments(alns)[[2]], 1:5)
#> [1] NA NA NA NA  1

# Charging the end gaps changes the overhang's score, and the aligner id says so:
charged <- proteins_align(list(c("MLLLPEPTIDE", "PEPTIDE")), end_gaps = "charged")
charged$records$score
#> [1] 24
charged$aligner_id
#> [1] "global-affine;BLOSUM62;open=11;extend=1;end-gaps=charged"
